units.locator: Article 1.6. Ensuring legality when applying measures of administrative coercion in connection with an administrative offence
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 1.6. Ensuring legality when applying measures of administrative coercion in connection with an administrative offence
units.label: Art. 1.6

units.locator: Article 1.6. Ensuring legality when applying measures of administrative coercion in connection with an administrative offence
units.text: 1. A person being held administratively liable may not be subjected to an administrative penalty or measures to secure proceedings in an administrative offence case except on the grounds and in accordance with the procedure established by law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 1.6

units.locator: Article 1.6. Ensuring legality when applying measures of administrative coercion in connection with an administrative offence
units.text: 2. An administrative penalty and measures to secure proceedings in an administrative offence case shall be applied in connection with an administrative offence by a body or official authorised to do so, within the competence of that body or official and in accordance with the law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 1.6

units.locator: Article 1.6. Ensuring legality when applying measures of administrative coercion in connection with an administrative offence
units.text: 3. When applying measures of administrative coercion, decisions and actions (inaction) that degrade human dignity are prohibited.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 1.6

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.label: Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.label: Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: 1. A person who has committed an administrative offence is subject to liability under the law in force at the time the administrative offence was committed.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: 2. A law that mitigates or abolishes administrative liability for an administrative offence or otherwise improves the position of the person who committed the administrative offence has retroactive effect, that is, it also applies to a person who committed an administrative offence before that law entered into force and in respect of whom the ruling imposing an administrative penalty has not been enforced. A law that establishes or increases administrative liability for an administrative offence or otherwise worsens the person's position has no retroactive effect.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: 2.1. Where provisions of a law abolishing administrative liability for an act and establishing criminal liability for the same act enter into force simultaneously, the person is subject to administrative liability under the law in force at the time the administrative offence was committed.
units.label: Part 2.1 Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.7. Operation of legislation on administrative offences in time
units.text: 3. Proceedings in an administrative offence case shall be conducted under the law in force at the time of the proceedings in that case.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 1.7

units.locator: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.text: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.label: Art. 1.8

units.locator: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.label: Art. 1.8

units.locator: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.text: 1. A person who has committed an administrative offence within the territory of the Russian Federation is subject to administrative liability in accordance with this Code or a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation on administrative offences, except in the cases provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 1.8

units.locator: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.text: 2. A person who has committed an administrative offence outside the Russian Federation is subject to administrative liability in accordance with this Code in the cases provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation and in the cases provided for by part 3 of this Article.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 1.8

units.locator: Article 1.8. Territorial operation of legislation on administrative offences
units.text: 3. A legal entity that has committed outside the Russian Federation an administrative offence provided for by Article 15.27.3 or 19.28 of this Code, and a person who has committed outside the Russian Federation an administrative offence provided for by Article 13.14.1, 13.15, 13.36, 13.37, 13.48, 17.13 or 19.34, part 3, 4 or 5 of Article 20.1, or Article 20.3.1, 20.3.2, 20.3.3, 20.3.4, 20.29 or 20.33 of this Code, or an administrative offence consisting in failure to pay, within the time limit provided for by this Code, an administrative fine imposed for such an administrative offence, are subject to administrative liability in accordance with this Code where those administrative offences are directed against the interests of the Russian Federation, and in the cases provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation, provided that those persons have not been held criminally or administratively liable for the corresponding acts in a foreign state.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 1.8

units.locator: Chapter 2. Administrative offences and administrative liability
units.text: Chapter 2. Administrative offences and administrative liability
units.label: Chapter 2. Administrative offences and administrative liability

units.locator: Chapter 2. Administrative offences and administrative liability
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Chapter 2. ADMINISTRATIVE OFFENCES AND ADMINISTRATIVE LIABILITY
units.label: Chapter 2. Administrative offences and administrative liability · “Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.…”

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.label: Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.label: Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: 1. An administrative offence is an unlawful, culpable act (omission) of an individual or a legal entity for which administrative liability is established by this Code or by the laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation on administrative offences.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: 2. A legal entity is found guilty of committing an administrative offence if it is established that it had the opportunity to comply with the rules and standards for the breach of which administrative liability is provided for by this Code or the laws of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation, but that entity did not take all measures within its power to comply with them.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: 3. The imposition of an administrative penalty on a legal entity does not release the guilty individual from administrative liability for the offence, just as holding an individual administratively or criminally liable does not release the legal entity from administrative liability for the offence, except in the cases provided for by parts 4 and 5 of this Article.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: 4. A legal entity is not subject to administrative liability for an administrative offence for which an official or another employee of that legal entity has been held administratively liable, or its sole executive body having the status of a legal entity has been held administratively liable, if that legal entity took all measures provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation to comply with the rules and standards for the breach of which administrative liability is provided for, except in the cases provided for by part 5 of this Article.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.1. Administrative offence
units.text: 5. If a legal entity has been given an administrative penalty for an administrative offence in the form of an administrative fine determined in accordance with point 3 or 5 of part 1 of Article 3.5 of this Code, an official or another employee of that legal entity, or its sole executive body having the status of a legal entity, is not subject to administrative liability.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 2.1

units.locator: Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.text: Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.label: Art. 2.2

units.locator: Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.label: Art. 2.2

units.locator: Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.text: 1. An administrative offence is deemed to have been committed intentionally if the person who committed it was aware of the unlawful nature of their act (omission), foresaw its harmful consequences and desired those consequences, or consciously allowed them to occur, or was indifferent to them.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.2

units.locator: Article 2.2. Forms of fault
units.text: 2. An administrative offence is deemed to have been committed through negligence if the person who committed it foresaw the possibility of harmful consequences of their act (omission), but presumptuously relied, without sufficient grounds, on preventing those consequences, or did not foresee the possibility of those consequences although they should and could have foreseen them.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.2

units.locator: Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.text: Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.label: Art. 2.3

units.locator: Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.label: Art. 2.3

units.locator: Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.text: 1. A person who has reached the age of sixteen years at the time of committing an administrative offence is subject to administrative liability.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.3

units.locator: Article 2.3. Age at which administrative liability arises
units.text: 2. Having regard to the specific circumstances of the case and information about the person who committed an administrative offence between the ages of sixteen and eighteen years, the commission for minors' affairs and the protection of their rights may release that person from administrative liability and apply to that person a corrective measure provided for by federal legislation on the protection of the rights of minors.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.3

units.locator: Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.text: Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.label: Art. 2.4

units.locator: Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.label: Art. 2.4

units.locator: Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.text: An official is subject to administrative liability where that official commits an administrative offence in connection with failure to perform, or improper performance of, their official duties.
units.label: Art. 2.4 · “An official is subject to administrative liability where that…”

units.locator: Article 2.4. Administrative liability of officials
units.text: Note. For the purposes of this Code, an official means a person who permanently, temporarily or under special authority performs the functions of a representative of public authority, that is, is vested, in accordance with the procedure established by law, with directive powers over persons who are not subordinate to them in an official capacity, as well as a person performing organisational and managerial or administrative and economic functions in state bodies, bodies of state extra-budgetary funds of the Russian Federation, local self-government bodies, state and municipal organisations, and also in the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation, other troops and military formations of the Russian Federation. Managers and other employees of other organisations and insolvency practitioners who have committed administrative offences in connection with the performance of organisational and managerial or administrative and economic functions, as well as members of boards of directors (supervisory boards), collegiate executive bodies (management boards, directorates), counting commissions, audit commissions (auditors), liquidation commissions of legal entities, managers of organisations exercising the powers of the sole executive bodies of other organisations, individuals who are founders (members) of legal entities, and managers of organisations exercising the powers of the sole executive bodies of organisations that are founders of legal entities, who have committed administrative offences provided for by parts 5 - 7, 11 and 16 of Article 7.30.3, Articles 9.22, 13.25, 14.24, 14.25, 14.56, part 3 of Article 14.57, Articles 14.61, 14.63, 14.64, 15.17 - 15.22, 15.23.1, 15.24.1, 15.25, 15.26.1, 15.26.2, 15.29 - 15.31, 15.37.1, 15.38, 15.49, parts 9 and 9.1 of Article 19.5 and Articles 19.7.3 and 19.7.12 of this Code, bear administrative liability as officials. Persons performing the functions of a member of a commission for the procurement of goods, works and services to meet state and municipal needs, contract managers and employees of a contract service who have committed administrative offences provided for by Articles 7.30.1 - 7.30.3, parts 7 and 7.1 of Article 19.5 and Article 19.7.2 of this Code bear administrative liability as officials. Persons performing functions related to organising and conducting procurement in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation on the procurement of goods, works and services by certain types of legal entities, including members of a procurement commission, who have committed administrative offences provided for by Article 7.30.4 and part 7.2 of Article 19.5 of this Code bear administrative liability as officials. Persons performing the functions of a member of a licensing commission who have committed an administrative offence provided for by Article 19.6.2 of this Code bear administrative liability as officials. Persons carrying on business without forming a legal entity who have committed administrative offences bear administrative liability as officials unless this Code provides otherwise. Persons performing functions related to organising and conducting tendering procedures that are mandatory under the legislation of the Russian Federation, including members of a tender commission or an auction commission, who have committed administrative offences provided for by Article 7.30.5 of this Code bear administrative liability as officials. Persons carrying out activities in the field of fire risk assessment (fire safety auditing) who have committed administrative violations provided for by part 9 of Article 20.4 of this Code bear administrative liability as officials. Persons carrying out activities involving the design of fire safety systems for buildings and structures that have been commissioned, who have committed administrative offences provided for by parts 10 and 11 of Article 20.4 of this Code, bear administrative liability as officials. Individuals carrying out expert examination activities in the field of the procurement of goods, works and services to meet state and municipal needs, who have committed an administrative offence provided for by Article 7.32.6 of this Code, bear administrative liability as officials.
units.label: Art. 2.4 · “Note. For the purposes of this Code, an official means a person…”

units.locator: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.text: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.label: Art. 2.5

units.locator: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.label: Art. 2.5

units.locator: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.text: 1. For administrative offences other than those provided for by part 2 of this Article, military personnel, citizens called up for military training, and employees holding special ranks in the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation, internal affairs bodies, the National Guard troops of the Russian Federation, bodies and institutions of the penal enforcement system, compulsory enforcement bodies of the Russian Federation, the State Fire Service and customs authorities bear disciplinary liability in accordance with federal laws and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation governing their military service (service) and status.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.5

units.locator: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.text: 2. For administrative offences provided for by Articles 5.1, 5.3 - 5.26, 5.45 - 5.50, 5.52, 5.56, 6.3, 7.30.1 - 7.30.3, Chapter 8, Article 11.16 (in respect of breaches of fire safety requirements outside the place of military service (service) or military training), Chapter 12, Article 14.9, part 7 of Article 14.32, Chapters 15 and 16, Articles 17.3, 17.7 - 17.9, parts 1 and 3 of Article 17.14, Articles 17.15, 18.1 - 18.4, parts 2.1, 2.6 and 7 of Article 19.5, Article 19.7.2, part 5 of Article 19.8, Article 19.12, Article 20.4 (in respect of breaches of fire safety requirements outside the place of military service (service) or military training) and part 1 of Article 20.25 of this Code, the persons specified in part 1 of this Article bear administrative liability on general grounds, except in the cases provided for by part 3 of this Article.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.5

units.locator: Article 2.5. Administrative liability of military personnel, citizens called up for military training and persons holding special ranks
units.text: 3. For administrative offences provided for by part 2 of this Article consisting in non-compliance with mandatory requirements, assessment of compliance with which is the subject of state control (supervision) whose organisation and conduct are regulated in accordance with part 6 of Article 2 of Federal Law No. 248-FZ of 31 July 2020 'On State Control (Supervision) and Municipal Control in the Russian Federation', the persons specified in part 1 of this Article bear disciplinary liability if they committed those administrative offences at facilities subject to the corresponding types of state control (supervision) and supervised by the federal executive bodies in which those persons perform military service (service) or military training.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 2.5

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.label: Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.label: Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: 1. Foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities that have committed administrative offences within the territory of the Russian Federation are subject to administrative liability on general grounds.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: 2. Foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities that have committed administrative offences provided for by part 2 of Article 8.16, Articles 8.17 - 8.20 and 11.7.1 and part 2 of Article 19.4 of this Code on the continental shelf or in the exclusive economic zone of the Russian Federation are subject to administrative liability on general grounds.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: 2.1. A foreign legal entity that has committed outside the Russian Federation an administrative offence provided for by Article 15.27.3 or 19.28 of this Code and directed against the interests of the Russian Federation, or a foreign citizen, stateless person or foreign legal entity that has committed outside the Russian Federation an administrative offence provided for by Article 13.14.1, 13.15, 13.36, 13.37, 13.48, 17.13 or 19.34, part 3, 4 or 5 of Article 20.1, or Article 20.3.1, 20.3.2, 20.3.3, 20.3.4, 20.29 or 20.33 of this Code and directed against the interests of the Russian Federation, or an administrative offence consisting in failure to pay, within the time limit provided for by this Code, an administrative fine imposed for such an administrative offence, is subject to administrative liability on general grounds.
units.label: Part 2.1 Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6. Administrative liability of foreign citizens, stateless persons and foreign legal entities
units.text: 3. The question of administrative liability of a foreign citizen who enjoys immunity from the administrative jurisdiction of the Russian Federation under federal laws and international treaties of the Russian Federation and who has committed an administrative offence within the territory of the Russian Federation shall be resolved in accordance with the rules of international law.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 2.6

units.locator: Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.text: Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.label: Art. 2.6.1

units.locator: Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.label: Art. 2.6.1

units.locator: Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.text: 1. Owners (possessors) of vehicles shall be held administratively liable for administrative offences in the field of environmental protection and the use of natural resources (in respect of the administrative offences provided for by parts 3.1 - 3.4 of Article 8.2 of this Code), administrative offences in the field of road traffic, and administrative offences in the field of territorial improvement, and administrative offences consisting in failure to comply with the procedure for paying for the passage of a vehicle along toll public motor roads of regional, intermunicipal and local significance, private public motor roads, toll sections of public motor roads of regional, intermunicipal and local significance, and toll sections of private public motor roads, as provided for by the laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, committed with the use of vehicles, where those administrative offences are recorded by special technical devices operating in automatic mode and having photographic, cinematographic or video-recording functions, or by photographic, cinematographic or video-recording equipment.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.6.1

units.locator: Article 2.6.1. Administrative liability of owners (possessors) of vehicles
units.text: 2. The owner (possessor) of a vehicle shall be released from administrative liability if, when an appeal against a ruling in an administrative offence case issued in accordance with part 3 of Article 28.6 of this Code is considered, the information contained in the appeal is confirmed that, at the time the administrative offence was recorded, the vehicle was in the possession or use of another person or had by that time ceased to be in the owner's (possessor's) possession as a result of unlawful acts of other persons.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.6.1

units.locator: Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.text: Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.label: Art. 2.6.2

units.locator: Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.label: Art. 2.6.2

units.locator: Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.text: 1. Owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property shall be held administratively liable for administrative offences in the field of territorial improvement provided for by the laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, in respect of the maintenance, operation, relocation, conversion or destruction of territorial improvement facilities, where those administrative offences are recorded by special technical devices operating in automatic mode and having photographic, cinematographic or video-recording functions, or by photographic, cinematographic or video-recording equipment.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 2.6.2

units.locator: Article 2.6.2. Administrative liability of owners or other possessors of land plots or other immovable property
units.text: 2. The owner or other possessor of a land plot or other immovable property shall be released from administrative liability if, when an appeal against a ruling in an administrative offence case issued in accordance with part 3 of Article 28.6 of this Code is considered, the information contained in the appeal is confirmed that, at the time the administrative offence was recorded, the land plot or other immovable property was in the possession or use of another person, or that the administrative offence was committed as a result of unlawful acts of other persons and the owner or other possessor of the land plot or other immovable property had no opportunity to prevent the administrative offence or had taken all measures within their power to prevent it.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 2.6.2

units.locator: Article 2.7. Extreme necessity
units.text: Article 2.7. Extreme necessity
units.label: Art. 2.7

units.locator: Article 2.7. Extreme necessity
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.7. Extreme necessity
units.label: Art. 2.7

units.locator: Article 2.7. Extreme necessity
units.text: The causing of harm by a person to interests protected by law in a state of extreme necessity does not constitute an administrative offence, that is, where the harm is caused to eliminate a danger directly threatening that person or their rights, other persons or their rights, or the interests of society or the state protected by law, if the danger could not be eliminated by other means and the harm caused is less significant than the harm prevented.
units.label: Art. 2.7 · text

units.locator: Article 2.8. Mental incapacity
units.text: Article 2.8. Mental incapacity
units.label: Art. 2.8

units.locator: Article 2.8. Mental incapacity
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.8. Mental incapacity
units.label: Art. 2.8

units.locator: Article 2.8. Mental incapacity
units.text: An individual who, at the time of committing unlawful acts (omissions), was in a state of mental incapacity, that is, was unable to understand the factual nature and unlawfulness of their acts (omissions) or to control them because of a chronic mental disorder, a temporary mental disorder, dementia or another pathological mental condition, is not subject to administrative liability.
units.label: Art. 2.8 · text

units.locator: Article 2.9. Possibility of release from administrative liability where an administrative offence is of minor significance
units.text: Article 2.9. Possibility of release from administrative liability where an administrative offence is of minor significance
units.label: Art. 2.9

units.locator: Article 2.9. Possibility of release from administrative liability where an administrative offence is of minor significance
units.text: Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.9. Possibility of release from administrative liability where an administrative offence is of minor significance
units.label: Art. 2.9

units.locator: Article 2.9. Possibility of release from administrative liability where an administrative offence is of minor significance
units.text: Where an administrative offence committed is of minor significance, the judge, body or official authorised to decide the administrative offence case may release the person who committed it from administrative liability and limit the response to an oral admonition.
units.label: Art. 2.9 · text
